order: Update the release changelog to record what the first hour of testing actually found. Name the four runner faults that surfaced and were fixed in this release. Those faults are the shell-launch fault and a path-comparison guarantee that failed under symlinks. They also include a refusal path that wrote before it objected. The fourth is a sweep step that under-reported its own scope. Note the one negative-control check that reports itself inconclusive under one platform's shell. That note keeps a future reader from mistaking it for a passing proof. Add a field-validation line documenting the shim case that testing can prove. That case cannot be staged against a real user's PATH directly. Bring the changelog's stated check count into sync with the suite's actual total. Move it from ninety-four to exactly ninety-six to match reality. Keep the change confined to documentation only, touching nothing in the source or test code.
claims: We recorded the four cross-platform runner faults found in early testing. Continuous integration surfaced them during its first hour, and this release fixed each one. We also noted the one negative control that reports inconclusive under one platform's shell. A field-validation line was added for the shim case integration testing can prove. That case cannot be staged on a real user's PATH directly. The change was documentation only, affecting three files with fifty-four added lines and ten removed. Check counts were synced from 94 to exactly 96, matching the suite's current total.
